John — thanks, and great question. Short answers up front:  

- License boundary: Redwood supports a limited runtime license for private deployments that permits operation of our inference runtime within a customer-managed VPC. The license is non-exclusive and scoped to the customer environment(s) specified in the Order Form. We usually capture the scope as "Deployment License: runtime binaries and configuration to operate Redwood Inference in Customer-controlled infrastructure." We can tighten wording if you need it limited to a single VPC/region.

- Evidence and audits: We provide an audit evidence package for Private deployments that includes: signed deployment attestation, configuration snapshot (metadata, not customer data), and a reproducible build manifest for the runtime and model artifact hashes. For regulated customers we can also provide a time-stamped snapshot on a cadence (quarterly) and support an onsite/remote audit under NDA.

- Escrow options: We have worked with third-party escrow agents for code/runtime escrow; we can share recommended providers and a typical setup timeline (~4–6 weeks for escrow contract + verification).

I attached a draft redline of the MSA (v2) for your internal review and cc'ing our legal and contracts leads to align on specifics and options. Would you be available for a 30-minute sync Friday 11/12 to walk through the attestation items? If that works I will have Aditya and Laura on the call.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Team — following the sync with John this morning, I pulled together a short comment matrix for legal/controls. High level notes (see attached matrix):

1) License scope: we should accept language that permits running our runtime in customer-managed infrastructure but add a clause that the license is limited to the runtime and excluded items (no transfer of model IP, no rights to redistribute beyond customer's environment). Proposed language: "Customer is granted a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to operate the Redwood Inference runtime within Customer-controlled infrastructure for the Term."

2) Custody & attestations: agree to quarterly signed deployment attestations (metadata + manifest sha256) and a one-time deployment verification during onboarding. Do NOT provide customer data snapshots. We should add a clause limiting Redwood's obligation to attestations of provisioning & runtime binaries only.

3) Escrow: offer an optional third-party code escrow for the runtime and build manifest; require MedAssist to execute escrow contract and cover escrow fees. We should recommend two escrow agents we have used (details in matrix).

4) Audit access: propose remote evidence package first; for onsite audits, require reasonable notice, scope-limiting, and Redwoods' personnel and travel fees if beyond standard inspection window.

5) Order Form: confirm environments (prod/staging) and per-region caps; recommend adding a single-sentence table in the Order Form that names the allowed VPCs/regions to avoid ambiguity.

I'll attach the legal_comment_matrix.xlsx with redline snippets. If this approach looks good I'll incorporate the exact contract language and hand it back to Tessa/Laura to send to MedAssist.

Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
